correctness.rationale: Section 3.5 of arXiv:2311.14206 defines the sketched harmonic quotient. Orthogonally decomposing v against Av reduces its reciprocal exactly to a shifted Student t variable with s degrees of freedom. Its continuous positive density at zero proves both signed 1/t tails, divergent positive and negative first moments, and the exact p<1 threshold. Conditional on every nonzero compact interval of sketch norms, the reciprocal retains a positive normal density at zero. The exceptional eigenvector case is deterministic. The actual packaged verify.py replays pathwise Gaussian identities, density, sign and tail tests; simulation is not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Original sketched harmonic Ritz definition, scalar equation and SVD stabilization are in Burke–Güttel–Soodhalter, arXiv:2311.14206, Section 3.5. The source provides no probabilistic classification of the scalar harmonic value. The Gaussian-sketched FOM analysis of Güttel–Schweitzer, arXiv:2208.11447, Section 2, yields related but different Galerkin correction ratios; the Palitta–Schweitzer–Simoncini sketched Ritz analysis, arXiv:2306.06481, Section 6, treats outlying Ritz values and matrix-function errors. Familiar reciprocal Student and Galerkin-pole reasoning informs the proof but does not explicitly state this harmonic extraction law, its two sign-tail constants and norm-screening persistence. Equivalence with an unknown Gaussian generalized quotient theorem is a residual risk.
residual_risks: A generalized Gaussian Rayleigh-quotient distribution could imply the scalar Student reduction in equivalent notation.
An analogous Gaussian-sketched Galerkin pole mechanism is known; the method-specific harmonic eigenvalue implication requires differentiation and has not been externally validated.

The plausible 2026 sketched harmonic Arnoldi paper (arXiv:2607.10354) could not be inspected in full; available abstract suggests different convergence questions, but overlap is not definitively excluded.

value.rationale: Harmonic Ritz spectral values are used to choose recycling/deflation directions. The result is an exact reliability limit not captured by mere subspace-vector singular values: for every finite sketch size, even after conditioning on arbitrarily tight positive norm bounds, a one-vector harmonic Ritz estimate has both sign errors and infinite positive/negative first moments. It gives exact sharp tail constants and a complete p-moment classification, identifying the need for a cross-angle safeguard rather than norm-only SVD screening. No solver divergence claim is made.
